# FamilyQuant 1.5.0.6 feature ledger

Contract for 2.0. Only Paulo may authorize DROP. KEEP preserves behavior; IMPROVE preserves the function while its presentation changes.
Per-row receipts and current audit commands are documented in `docs/FEATURE-EVIDENCE.md`.
VERIFIED states proposed by a worker remain provisional until independent review and the desk's merged green gate.
Retained rows start OPEN. A planned check is not evidence that behavior passed. Close a retained row only after its owner records an executed test or an inspected render and reviewer approval. Approved DROP rows record Paulo's decision as evidence, without claiming their implementation is removed yet.
Approved exception: Paulo via orchestrator M4, 2026-11-01 11:20:38: retire the De Novo Extract areas and Partition ion current sections in 2.0; 1.5 keeps them. Attribute to families stays and its CSV moves to Results in C11.
DROP covers the two frozen XAML section subtrees and their exclusive view handlers/tooltips. Shared extraction/partition engines, test seams, explanatory science and Attribute to families remain preserved. The guard rejects DROP outside that scope. Actual retirement is C11.

Frozen source: `e9b73064d8ff19b2fde3e3231240b636a64c0a91` in the old FamilyQuant repository, matching the read-only reference README. The frozen app and tests are in `D:/FamilyQuant-data/reference-1.5.0.6`.
Source hashes, per-file counts and exact observations: `docs/feature-ledger-scan.json`. Scan includes all product XAML and C# files, including code-only windows, event wiring, key handling, help, option copy, export/storage builders and file-extension literals. Zero-observation files remain in the manifest.
XAML: one control row plus each behavioral/copy/tooltip attribute. C#: literal tokens in UI/help/option/export code, every file-format literal, code-created controls, event hooks, handler definitions and key references. Literal fragments remain separate and retain source syntax; internal strings are deliberately over-included. This is a static preservation inventory, not a proof that each code branch is reachable.
Unicode in frozen copy is escaped so old punctuation and icons are recorded without introducing them into new UI. Formatting and color attributes are excluded; they are not preserved appearance requirements.

Regenerate from a clean source export of that commit: `FamilyQuant.Tests.exe --feature-ledger-generate <frozen-source-root> <2.0-repo-root>`. Never regenerate from moving 2.0 source. The default suite checks source counts, stable IDs, exact row coverage, dispositions and check targets. When `FAMILYQUANT_LEDGER_REFERENCE_SOURCE` points to the source export, it also repeats the scan and compares every observation and source hash.
Render targets refer to `ScreenHarness.Screens`, captured with `--screens <output>`, in both themes and sizes. Test targets name existing suite methods in the relevant area. A target identifies where the owner must check that fact; it does not assert that the current method covers every detail. A render checks visible presentation only; interactions, numbers and compatibility still need executable checks before closure. Extend or replace a broad target with the exact assertion before marking a row VERIFIED.
Release gate: `FamilyQuant.Tests.exe --feature-ledger-release-check` fails until every retained row is VERIFIED with evidence. Authorized DROP rows use APPROVED_DROP, which records a decision, not a completed UI removal. The normal quick suite permits OPEN rows during development. Regeneration resets retained rows to OPEN; preserve reviewed evidence when updating the scanner.

## Added contracts after the frozen source

These are additions, not replacements or drops of frozen FQ15 observations. The named DefaultSuite
checks guard the contract and its presence. Executed native proof is recorded separately for review;
adding this row does not change any frozen disposition, scan hash or receipt verification state.
